sections.h2: Which ways of selling a Cedar Park house are open to me?
sections.html:
A Cedar Park owner can work with an agent, manage the sale personally, or accept an investor's cash purchase with no repairs. Condition and timing decide which suits you.

  • With an agent: broad buyer exposure, plus showings, lender appraisals and post-inspection repair asks.
  • Self-managed: you price the house and coordinate the contract with a title company.
  • Investor purchase: built for deferred maintenance, occupied rentals, estates or a tight calendar.

Three Cedar Park items surface in nearly every sale: the permit record, any short-term rental registration, and the tax account.

sections.h2: How did Cedar Park grow from a railroad stop into a city?
sections.html:
Cedar Park grew from a ranch settlement into an Austin suburb that was incorporated in 1973. The Texas Historical Commission marker, dedicated in 1985 and set outside the public library at 550 Discovery Blvd., tells it: in 1873 a couple bought a large tract rich in cedar and limestone, a post office opened in 1874 under the name Running Brushy, and the railroad arrived in 1882 when the name changed to Bruggerhoff. Five years later the present name was adopted.

The marker adds that the founder opened a cedar yard to sell posts as barbed wire spread, that the early twentieth century brought little growth, and that by 1960 nearly all traces of the old community had disappeared. Austin's growth in the 1970s pulled people north. The city's economic development group now calls Cedar Park the third largest city in the Austin metro and a part of Williamson County.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and county handle my Cedar Park property taxes?
sections.html:
Your latest tax statement names the county and the appraisal district that carry your parcel. Cedar Park describes itself as part of Williamson County, whose Central Appraisal District values property there.

Texas levies no state property tax, so each local unit sets its own rate. Appraised values are set on January 1, a lien for that year attaches the same day, and bills follow in October. Per the Comptroller, a penalty and interest begin to build once tax goes delinquent on February 1.

For current rates, call the Williamson County tax office and request the adopted figure for each unit on your bill.

sections.h2: How do the homestead exemption and the 10 percent cap work in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
Cedar Park homeowners get a brake on rising assessments, and the brake stays with the owner rather than the house. Williamson CAD says a home qualifies in the second full year the exemption has been on the property for the same owner, and that increases in existing assessed value are held to 10 percent a year even when market value climbs faster.

The district also says the cap does not transfer with ownership, so a buyer starts fresh and may see a bigger jump than you did. Useful points from the district:

  • You apply once; the exemption stays unless you move or add another one.
  • A Texas driver license or ID showing your current address is required.
  • Processing can take up to 90 days.
  • The chief appraiser re-checks each homestead exemption within every five tax years.

sections.h2: What does Cedar Park's short-term rental registration mean for sellers?
sections.html:
If your Cedar Park house is rented for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, City Council's April 2026 ordinance applies. Registration became required on October 1, 2026, costs $100 a year, and ties into Hotel Occupancy Tax reporting under Chapter 10 of the City Code. The city estimates about 200 active short-term rentals.

A buyer who plans to keep renting will ask whether the registration exists and whether tax was remitted. The city lists Development Services at 512-401-5100 for registration and Utility Billing at 512-401-5300 for hotel tax payments, and registered owners can watch remittance through an online portal. The city says registration exists so it can count and locate these rentals, support safety, and make sure the hotel tax is collected. Gather the confirmation and remittance history before you list, because they are the first things a rental buyer asks to see.

sections.h2: What permit and repair rules should I check before selling in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
Open permits are a common reason a Cedar Park closing pauses. The city runs permits through the MGO Connect portal, and Development Services is at the City Hall campus, 450 Cypress Creek Road, Building 1. Its zoning map tool, CPAtlas, lets you type in an address to see zoning.

sections.h2: What if the Cedar Park house is inherited, in foreclosure or has a tenant?
sections.html:
Each situation runs on a Texas clock.

  • Foreclosure: the borrower gets 20 days from the default notice to reinstate, and auctions take place at the courthouse on first Tuesdays.
  • Inheritance: a will can be probated for four years after death, and the small estate affidavit tops out at $75,000 excluding homestead and exempt property.
  • Tenant: a landlord normally gives 3 days of written notice to vacate before filing in justice court, unless the lease sets another period.

A buyer can take on these issues, but the title company still needs proof of who may sign. A Williamson County probate attorney can say which paper fits.

sections.h2: What should I do first if I want to sell my Cedar Park house quickly?
sections.html:
Five checks, done in order, show you which sale routes are realistically open to you.

  • Pull the tax statement and confirm the district and any balance.
  • Ask Development Services whether any permit on the address is open.
  • Get your mortgage payoff figure.
  • If the house was a short-term rental, collect registration and hotel tax records.
  • Name your deadline, such as a sale date or a move, and tell every buyer you talk to about it.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cedar Park house with an open building permit?
faqs.a: Yes, though it complicates the sale. A Cedar Park permit lapses after 180 days without a start or with work stopped. Call Development Services at 512-401-5100 about the record, or sell to a buyer willing to take the open item.

faqs.q: Must my Cedar Park short-term rental be registered before a sale?
faqs.a: If guests stay 30 days or fewer, registration has been required since October 1, 2026, at $100 a year. A buyer planning to keep renting will want the registration and your hotel occupancy tax records.

faqs.q: Does my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Williamson CAD states the cap does not transfer with ownership. The new owner applies for an exemption of their own, and the cap counts from their first full year.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent on February 1, per the Texas Comptroller. For the exact balance on your account, call the Williamson County tax office.

faqs.q: What does the Texas foreclosure timeline look like?
faqs.a: A default notice starts a 20-day reinstatement window. After that, the lender gives notice of sale, and the auction happens at the courthouse on a first Tuesday.
